ps.title: PlayStation UI
ps.summary: The PlayStation website reimagined as something you play like a console, with △ ○ ✕ □ as the real navigation.
ps.role: Research, concept, UI, design system, prototype. Built in Figma.
method: Studied 20 websites: 10 from the same industry, 10 with standout design.
Built at least 3 structurally different options for every screen before picking one.
Put each screen next to big-brand sites and fixed wherever it lost.
ps.output: 10 screens: Boot, Home (a single no-scroll screen with 4 entry points), Game Library, Game Detail (Ghost of Tsushima), PS5 Hardware, Search, Cart, Checkout, Save Data (1994 to 2020), Account. A system of 45 tokens, 10 text styles, components with every state, and a prototype driven by arrow keys, Enter and Esc.
ps.result: Self-assessed against 10 UI criteria: Home 80.5/100, Game Detail 83/100.
ps.disclaimer: Personal, non-commercial project. Not affiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment.
ps.coverAlt: PlayStation UI Home: one screen split into four by a large ✕, each quarter an entry point.
ps.img1Alt: Game Detail in its Ghost state.
ps.img2Alt: PS5 Hardware page: hold ✕ to power on the console.
ps.img2Cap: PS5 Hardware: hold ✕ to power on

case.context: A brief I set myself: what if the PlayStation website worked like the console itself? △ ○ ✕ □ stop being decoration and become the way you actually move around.
case.methodIntro: Three habits that kept the project from drifting on instinct:
screens: Home: one no-scroll screen with 4 entry points
system: A prototype driven by arrow keys, Enter and Esc
case.resultNote: These are self-assessed scores against 10 UI criteria, not results from user testing.
case.reflection: The scores are my own. Next time I would put the keyboard prototype in front of real users before scoring it, so someone else checks the numbers.

karsia.title: KARSIA Retreat Ninh Bình
karsia.summary: Reworking the interface of a live website from client feedback, while touching as little code as possible.
karsia.role: UI/UX, designed in Figma before handing over to development.
method: Audited the Figma file and turned 14 loose copies of the header and footer into components.
Set up variables: 10 colours and 41 text styles.
Split 35 pieces of client feedback into 42 tasks, each tagged by how much code it would take.
Placed every “after” directly below its “before” so the client could compare.
karsia.output: Designed the missing pages: a 124-photo gallery, a booking popup, the open menu and an article template. Prototyped the menu and booking flows.
karsia.triageTitle: 42 tasks, sorted by cost to code
karsia.highlight: Sorting feedback by code cost made the trade-offs obvious to the client: 29 of the 42 tasks were light fixes.
karsia.coverAlt: KARSIA’s “Our services” block after the redesign: restaurant, bar and pool photos with descriptions.

case.context: A resort website that was already live. The client sent 35 pieces of feedback on the interface, with one constraint: change as little code as possible.
case.triageStory: Instead of working through them one by one, I split the 35 comments into 42 tasks and tagged each by how much code it would take. One look told the client what could ship now and what would cost real effort.
outputs: Prototype of the menu and booking flows
Header and footer as components, replacing 14 loose copies
case.result: The client received a list of 42 tasks tagged by code cost, and for every change an “after” placed directly below its “before”.
case.resultNote: The hero in Figma is still a grey box waiting for the resort’s original photo, so it is not shown here.
case.reflection: The hero is still waiting on the original photo. Next time I would ask for every original asset up front, so no grey boxes reach the handoff file.
case.g4Alt: Shared components: navigation, footer and icon set.

idea.title: 2IDEA
idea.summary: A full redesign of 2idea.com.vn that also folds two sub-brands, Lịch Bông Sen and Quà tặng 24K, into one system.
idea.role: UI/UX, information architecture, prototype. Built in Figma.
method: Studied 9 international print and gifting brands (MOO, Pentagram, Papier, Moleskine…) and shipped 26 recommendations from them.
Reviewed 10 Lunar New Year gift sites before designing the Tết gifts section.
Edited the tone of voice across 372 passages.
Ran automated checks on 7,988 desktop links and 3,153 mobile links: none broken. Tested at 360 and 430 px: no overflow.
idea.output: A product spec picker with a running estimate, a Tết section where you build your own gift box, search in place of a menu bar, and an AI assistant button.
idea.result: Self-assessed at 75/100 on desktop and 70/100 on mobile. What holds it back: the photos are not real product shots yet, and spacing does not follow a 4 px grid.
idea.coverAlt: Top of the 2IDEA desktop homepage: menu bar and a design-and-print banner.
idea.stripAlt: The full 2IDEA desktop homepage, from banner to footer.
idea.stripCap: Desktop homepage, scroll inside the frame to see it all
idea.mobileAlt: Three 2IDEA mobile screens: Home, Menu and AI assistant.

case.context: 2IDEA is a design, print and gifting company. The brief: redesign all of 2idea.com.vn and bring two sub-brands, Lịch Bông Sen and Quà tặng 24K, into the same system.
highlights: A product spec picker with a running estimate
A Tết gifts section where you build your own box
Search in place of a menu bar
case.reflection: The two things holding it back are clear: the photos are not real yet, and spacing does not follow a 4 px grid. Next time I would set the 4 px grid on the very first screen and get real product photos before building.
